content:
Figure I'd post this here. Currentlly, docs#Topology.scottHausdorff topology has a parameter D : Set (Set α) which essentially restricts the sets whose directed suprema we care about. It was added in #16523 by Christopher Hoskins (who we all miss dearly), and as far as I can see it seems to be used only to prove that a docs#OmegaCompletePartialOrder.ωScottContinuous function is the same as a continuous function on the Scott-Hausdorff topology restricted to ω-chains.

In the case D = univ, the resulting topology is simply the topology whose open sets are docs#DirSupInacc (just as in the literature). We have a definition docs#DirSupInaccOn which relativizes the definition to a set D, but confusingly, in the general case these are not the open sets of the Scott-Hausdorff topology. The definition of Topology.scottHausdorff does not mention DirSupInaccOn at all; it works out so that every open set is DirSupInaccOn, but not all DirSupInaccOn sets are Scott-Hausdorff open. In fact, DirSupInaccOn isn't even closed under intersections in the general case, so it can't form a topology.

Now, if D is a lower set, all of this can be salvaged. In this case, DirSupInaccOn sets form a topology which can be proven equal to the one which Mathlib currently uses for Scott-Hausdorff. (I have Lean proofs of these facts)

My proposal then is to redefine docs#Topology.scottHausdorff as follows:

def scottHausdorff (α : Type*) (D : LowerSet (Set α)) [Preorder α] : TopologicalSpace α where
  IsOpen := DirSupInaccOn D
  isOpen_univ := DirSupInaccOn.univ
  isOpen_sUnion _ := DirSupInaccOn.sUnion
  isOpen_inter _ _ := DirSupInaccOn.inter D.lower'

Note that the ω-Scott continuous usage can be recovered by taking D as the lower closure of all ω-chains. The sets in this closure are either ω-chains or finite, but the latter are automatically closed under suprema, so it gives the same result as just taking all ω-chains.

Thoughts? cc. @Aaron Liu @Bhavik Mehta @Yaël Dillies

Hmm, something I just now notice is that whereas IsOpen s ↔ DirSupInacc D s in the Scott-Hausdorff topology seems to require D to be a lower set or some similar condition, IsOpen s ↔ IsUpperSet s ∧ DirSupInacc D s in the Scott topology is unconditional. So maybe the correct solution here is to keep the definition as is, but use an IsLowerSet D assumption throughout the Scott-Hausdorff API?
I think your very last solution is the correct one.
